title: Creation, Eden, and the Human Calling
theme: image-bearing / heavenly family / sacred space / rebel / last Adam
big: Yahweh alone creates humanity in his image to represent his rule on Earth. The Eden rebel attacks that vocation; Jesus fulfills and restores it as the last Adam.
question: What does Genesis say humans are created to be and do?
observe: Note who is speaking in Genesis 1:26 and what image/likeness language is doing.
Trace the human task in 1:28 and 2:15: rule, fill, work, keep.
Watch the serpent invert Yahweh word in 3:1-5.
Mark the first gospel hint in 3:15 and the exile from sacred space in 3:22-24.
Connect image-bearing with Psalm 8 and last-Adam language in Romans 5 and 1 Corinthians 15.
teacherMoves: Open with image as vocation, not merely ontology.
Read 1:26-28 slowly; ask who we are meant to represent.
Use Job 38:4-7 for heavenly family watching creation.
Guard against treating Eden as a mere orchard story.
Point ahead to Jesus as last Adam without skipping Genesis.
app: Live this week as an image-bearer: represent Yahweh rule in ordinary work, family, and speech.
guard: Do not reduce image of God to a list of human faculties while ignoring royal-priestly vocation.
response: Blessed are you, Yahweh; you made us to walk with you. Restore our calling in Messiah.

teacherOnly.label: teacher method — do not dump Rev 12 on the guys
p: [A] is the speaking נחש among the beasts in Genesis 3. [B] is later identification (Rev 12). The guys’ recap line “the nachash is a spiritual rebel” is [B]. Leave it. Do not dump Rev 12 onto the student recap.
Genesis does not open with a committee of gods making the world. Yahweh speaks, and it is. Light, land, living things, then humans. The verbs of making belong to him.

Job 38 sits beside that. When Yahweh laid the earth’s foundation, the morning stars sang and all the sons of God shouted. The heavenly family was already there as witness. They did not create. They watched.

items.b: “Let us make” is council language, not co-creators
p: Genesis 1:26: “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.” Yahweh is addressing the court around him. The next verse does the making in the singular: God created. The sons of God bear witness. They do not share the Creator’s throne.
That matches Job 38. The morning stars are there when the earth is laid. They are not the ones laying it.

items.b: Image (צֶלֶם tselem) is vocation, not a parts list
p: Humans are made in his image and likeness to represent his rule on the earth: be fruitful, fill, subdue, have dominion (1:26–28). Then 2:15: work it and keep it. Royal-priestly work in sacred space, not “you have a mind, therefore you are the image.”

Psalm 8 sings the same calling: crowned with glory and honor, given rule over the works of his hands. Romans 5 and 1 Corinthians 15 pick it up in the last Adam. The first man fails the vocation. Yeshua does not.
Not a children’s orchard. Yahweh is present. Two trees. A task. A real prohibition: of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day you eat of it you shall surely die.

When they are driven out, cherubim and a flaming sword guard the way to the tree of life (3:24). New guardians at the gate. The nachash is no longer in that post. The garden is not a metaphor God later abandoned. The text says they were sent out from it.

items.b: The nachash is a spiritual rebel
p: נָחָשׁ nachash. Later Scripture names that rebel Satan. Do not sand that down into “a snake in a garden story.” The Bible stacks this being across the book.

His craft is truth with a death-lie in it. “You will not surely die.” They do. The tree is the knowledge of good and evil. They did not yet know their sin the way they would after they took. Nakedness is both: they were unashamed, then they knew they were naked. Hebrew plays עָרוֹם arom (naked) against עָרוּם arum (crafty) in 2:25–3:1. That wordplay holds.
Eve added “do not touch,” which God did not say. The adversary works in the gap between what Yahweh said and what we start saying for him.
I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head. You will strike his heel.
Hebrew זֶרַע zera here is masculine. A he, not a vague they. That war is the rest of the book: seed against seed, the rebel’s line against the promised one. Week 2 is the next strike on that line.

Blameless, upright, feared Yahweh, turned from evil. Seven sons and three daughters. He would rise early and offer for them in case they had sinned in their hearts. The book wants you to know he is not being punished for a hidden crime.

A day came when the sons of God presented themselves before Yahweh, and the adversary was among them. Yahweh said, have you considered my servant Job. The adversary said Job only fears you because you hedged him. Stretch out your hand. Yahweh gave permission. He withheld Job’s life from the adversary. Testing is already there. Yahweh remains God. He is not on a leash.

items.b: The feast was not a wedding
p: Messengers in a pile: oxen and donkeys taken, fire on the sheep, Chaldeans on the camels. Then the one that is easy to misremember. Job’s sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother. Not a wedding that collapsed. A great wind from the wilderness. The house fell on the young people. They died.
Job tore his robe, shaved, fell, and worshiped. Yahweh gave, Yahweh took. Blessed be the name of Yahweh. He did not charge Yahweh with wrong.

items.b: Skin for skin, then the whirlwind
p: Another day in the council. Skin for skin. Yahweh allowed bone and flesh, not his life. Job sat in ashes with sores. His wife said curse God and die. He would not. Three friends sat seven days without a word, then wrecked it by insisting he must have sinned.

Job cursed his birth. He did not throw away God. He wanted the pressure to stop. Yahweh answered from the whirlwind: where were you when I laid the earth? When the morning stars sang and all the sons of God shouted. That is why this book is in Week 1. The council is already there when the world is made.

Yahweh restored Job. The friends had to ask Job to pray for them. He saw sons and daughters again. The first man in this story is not the last Adam. He is the template for a righteous sufferer under a God who is not on a leash.
Eden is not the only rebellion. Genesis 6: the sons of God, the daughters of men, the Nephilim, the flood, a remnant through Noah. The adversary’s host, and the sons of God in the days of Noah.
That is Week 2. Seed line. Watchers. Flood. The war announced in 3:15 does not pause.

title: Seed Line, Watchers, and Flood
thisWeek: Rebellion spreads past Eden. Yahweh judges the world by flood. He keeps a seed through Noah.
big: Rebellion spreads past Eden. Yahweh judges the world by flood. He keeps a seed through Noah.
student: Genesis 4:1-16; Genesis 6:1-22; Job 1:6 and Job 38:4-7; Genesis 8:20-9:17
question: How does rebellion spread, and what does Yahweh preserve?
observe: Genesis 4: two lines. Violence, and a seed that still calls on Yahweh.
Genesis 6:1-4 with Job 1:6 and 38:7: bene ha-elohim is the same phrase. Divine beings, not Sethite men.
Genesis 6:4 says “and also afterward.” We will meet that when Scripture brings it.
Genesis 6:3’s 120 years: hold both a countdown to the flood and the later human lifespan.
Noah after: a seed kept. Yahweh binds himself.
Older Hebrew copies from the desert confirm the reading. Extra cave books are labeled; they are not Torah.
Nimrod and Babel are next week. 1 Enoch is extra-biblical. Label it. It cannot overrule Genesis.
teacherMoves: Honor the group request: Watchers, Nephilim, afterward. Do not turn class into folklore hour.

Hold up their English Bible. Name where it came from (grandchild of Masoretic Hebrew; ESV sits in the KJV–RSV line). Then open Job 1:6 and Genesis 6:2 in Hebrew so bene ha-elohim is not a Sethite guess. English flattened this for a long time; do not let them hear “sons of Israel” here.
Read Genesis 6:1-8 aloud twice, then Job 1:6 and 38:7. Two lines in Genesis 4, then the flood, then a seed kept (8:20–9:17). Nimrod is next week. Do not open Genesis 10.

Watcher word is Daniel 4 (holy), not Enoch’s class-word for the rebels. Genesis 6 says sons of God. Jude 6 and 2 Peter 2:4: angels who left their habitation. Ranks: Job’s court sons of God vs the bound ones vs Daniel’s holy Watchers. Do not mash them.
If you mention Qumran: two piles. Scripture copies confirm. Extra books labeled. Do not send 1Q20 or 1 Enoch 106 in GroupMe.

1 Peter 3:20-21: later Scripture names the flood as the earth going through water; a remnant comes out. Walk Noah tonight. Do not start at the font or lecture baptism. Do not say “Messiah is the greater ark” as the opening frame — that puts baptism in front. Name 1 Peter 3 as the later line so they know where it lands.
If you tell the shining-Noah story, label it extra-biblical in the room, then land on Genesis 6:9. Do not send it in the group text.
app: Where rebellion looks overwhelming, cling to the God who preserves a people through judgment.
guard: Do not let giant-clan curiosity eclipse the gospel: flood is about Yahweh justice and mercy, not monster lore.
response: Yahweh, judge evil and keep a remnant. Hide us in Messiah, our ark.

studyApp.label: Nephilim & Giants in the study app
studyApp.note: Hebrew and the Nephilim file are here if you want them. Scripture on this page is enough for Sunday. 1 Enoch is labeled extra-biblical.

teacherOnly.h: Do not send this block to the group
p: This is teacher-only color. The guys’ page does not have it. If you use it in the room, say out loud that it is not Genesis.

teacherOnly.h: Two Lamechs. Do not mix them.
p: Cain’s Lamech is Genesis 4:23-24. He boasts of violence and of seventy-sevenfold vengeance. That is the Cain line after Eden.

Seth’s Lamech is Genesis 5:28-31. He fathers Noah and names him: this one will comfort us from our work and from the toil of our hands, because of the ground which Yahweh has cursed. That is the seed line.

teacherOnly.label: canonical — this is the proof
p: The word is Aramaic עִיר (ir), plural עִירִין (irin). Root = awake / wakeful. Strong’s H5894. It occurs ONLY in Daniel 4 in the whole Bible. English Bibles (ESV/KJV) print those sentences as 4:13, 4:17, 4:23. Ancient Texts / MT Aramaic numbering prints the same words as 4:10, 4:14, 4:20. Same עִיר / עִירִין. If you open the app to English 4:13 you will miss it. Use 4:10, 4:14, 4:20 in the app.
Daniel 4:13 (English) / 4:10 (MT): Nebuchadnezzar, on his bed, saw עִיר וְקַדִּישׁ, a Watcher and a holy one, coming down from heaven.
Daniel 4:17 (English) / 4:14 (MT): בִּגְזֵרַת עִירִין the sentence is by decree of the Watchers, and by word of the holy ones (קַדִּישִׁין), so the living know the Most High rules the kingdom of men.
Daniel 4:23 (English) / 4:20 (MT): Daniel restates the king’s sight: a Watcher and a holy one descending.
Those Watchers in Daniel 4 are holy. They execute the Most High’s decree against a proud king. They are not the Genesis 6 rebels.

Genesis 6:1-4 does not say Watcher. It says בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים. Stack Job 1:6 and 38:7 for the same phrase. Jude 6 and 2 Peter 2:4 speak of angels who left their habitation / sinned. They do not use the word Watcher. 1 Enoch uses ἐγρήγοροι / Watchers for the rebels. That is extra-biblical class-language mapped onto Genesis 6. Scripture’s own Watcher-word is Daniel 4, and there they are holy.

If you say Watcher in the room, open Daniel 4 so the guys hear it from Nebuchadnezzar (English 4:13 / app 4:10), then say Genesis 6 uses a different phrase. Do not let Enoch baptize Daniel’s holy Watcher as a demon. The Ancient Texts chapter study wrongly treats 1 Enoch as a second Hebrew-Bible Watcher occurrence. It is not. Daniel 4 is the only biblical use of the word. 1 Enoch is extra-biblical. Do not copy that error onto this page.

teacherOnly.label: EXTRA_BIBLICAL
p: Genesis does NOT say Noah’s face shone. Genesis 5:28-31: Seth’s Lamech names him Noah because this one will comfort us from our work and the toil of our hands, from the ground Yahweh cursed. That is the Bible.
Two extra-biblical witnesses, independent enough to take seriously as Second Temple memory, not as Torah:

1) 1 Enoch 106 (Book of Noah fragment): body white as snow and red as a rose, hair white as wool, eyes like the sun, the house glows when he opens them, he speaks righteousness. Lamech fears he is of the angels, not of him. Methuselah goes to Enoch. Enoch: in Jared’s generation they transgressed, united with women, flood is coming, this child is righteous, call him Noah, remnant. Label EXTRA_BIBLICAL.

2) Genesis Apocryphon 1Q20 (Qumran Cave 1, Aramaic). Col. 2: Lamech considers whether the pregnancy was of the Watchers and Holy Ones or the Nephilim. He makes Batenosh swear. She weeps and swears by the Great Holy One the seed is Lamech’s, not from any Watcher or heavenly being. Col. 5: Enoch says the child is from Lamech, not the heavenly beings; eyes shone like the sun. This is a Dead Sea scroll, not a medieval Ethiopic-only rumor.

Why it is worth knowing: the fear only exists if Genesis 6 is sons of God as heavenly beings. A Sethite reading has no reason for Lamech to suspect Watcher paternity. The story ALSO answers no: Noah is not mixed. That matches Genesis 6:8-9: Noah found favor, a righteous man, tamim in his generations, he walked with God.
Why we do not believe it as Moses: it is not in Genesis. 1 Enoch cannot overrule Scripture. Do not send it in GroupMe. If you tell it in the room, say out loud it is not Genesis, then land on 6:9.
Two Lamechs still: Cain’s Lamech Genesis 4:23-24 vs Seth’s Lamech Genesis 5:28-31. Do not mix them.

teacherOnly.h: QUMRAN AND ANCIENT TRANSLATIONS — WHY WE TRUST THEM
teacherOnly.label: teacher method — two piles, Scripture first
p: Two piles came out of the caves. Qumran, Judean desert, roughly 250 BC–70 AD. Finds from 1947 on. Pile one: copies of books we already have as Scripture — Hebrew, Aramaic, some Greek. Pile two: the community’s other books — Aramaic Enoch fragments, Genesis Apocryphon 1Q20, and the rest. They are not the same thing. Do not baptize pile two as Torah. Extra cave books are labeled. They are not Moses.

Why we trust pile one. Those Scripture copies are about a thousand years older than the medieval Masoretic copies most English Bibles rest on. Leningrad Codex: 1008 AD. When DSS and MT agree, the text was already stable. For Genesis 6:1–4 the Hebrew is not a DSS-versus-MT fight. Moses stands. The scrolls confirm him. We do not need Qumran to prove Genesis 6. We use it because it is an older witness of the same words.

Why pile two still matters without ruling. Those extra books show how Jews already read Genesis 6 before Jesus: heavenly beings, Watchers, fear of mixed seed. That is why the Lamech/Noah fear in 1Q20 and 1 Enoch 106 only exists if the sons of God are not Sethite men. The SHINING NOAH block on this page already has the story. Do not retell it here. Label EXTRA_BIBLICAL. They cannot overrule Genesis 6:9: Noah is righteous, tamim in his generations, he walked with God.

Ancient translations are a check, not a replacement of Hebrew. The LXX (Greek OT, 3rd–2nd c. BC) is a Jewish translation. The early church read its Old Testament in that Greek. Some LXX witnesses at Genesis 6:2 read angels of God (οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ) rather than sons of God — a translation that already heard heavenly beings. Later Targums (Aramaic) sometimes sand it to sons of nobles / judges. Name that as later human flattening. Do not follow it. Peshitta and Vulgate are later. Do not make them the spine.

When copies disagree, the load-bearing case is Deuteronomy 32:8. DSS and LXX: sons of God. Later MT: sons of Israel. That is Week 3 — nations at Babel. Do not teach Babel tonight. Name it so you know why we bother with scrolls at all: sometimes the older Hebrew copy preserves what a later copy smoothed. Tonight Genesis 6 does not need that fight. Next week we will.

Rule in the room. Scripture first: MT Genesis, Job 1:6 and 38:7, Daniel 4 Watcher — already on this page. DSS copies of Scripture = older witnesses. LXX = ancient Jewish check. 1 Enoch and 1Q20 = how they read Moses, not Moses. Where they agree with Genesis they thicken it. Where they do not, Genesis wins. Extra-biblical cannot overrule Scripture.

teacherOnly.h: WHERE OUR CURRENT TRANSLATION COMES FROM
teacherOnly.label: teacher method — English is a check, not the source
p: Guys open their own Bibles tonight. The study site reader has used Crossway ESV on Week 2 when it showed English. Ancient Texts Flow is KJV-keyed. English is a CHECK, not the source. Hebrew and Aramaic first. Never treat NIV, ESV, or KJV as equivalent to the Hebrew. Send them back to the words. Babel’s split already made every later tongue thinner.

Hold the chain short and true. Not a seminary lecture. (1) Moses and the prophets wrote in Hebrew. Daniel 4’s Watcher is Aramaic. That is the source. (2) Dead Sea Scrolls: Hebrew and Aramaic copies, roughly 250 BC–70 AD. Pile one confirms the Scripture text is already what we have. Pile two (1 Enoch fragments, Genesis Apocryphon 1Q20) is how that community read it. Labeled. Cannot overrule Genesis. (3) LXX: Jewish Greek translation, 3rd–2nd c. BC. The early church’s Old Testament in Greek. Some Genesis 6:2 copies: angels of God. Check, not replacement. (4) Masoretic Text: Jewish scribes, vowels and accents. The complete medieval copy is the Leningrad Codex, 1008 AD. This is the Hebrew base of almost every English OT. (5) Reformation English: Tyndale, Geneva, KJV 1611 went back to Hebrew and Greek, not Latin-only. KJV OT from the Rabbinic/Bomberg Hebrew (Ben Hayyim). KJV NT from the Textus Receptus. (6) What most of them hold tonight: ESV (Crossway, 2001) sits in the KJV–RSV lineage. OT from Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia, which is Leningrad Masoretic. NT Nestle-Aland. Formal, thinner than Hebrew. NIV and CSB are more thought-for-thought. Still English. Still downstream.

Why this week. They will hear “sons of God.” Some Bibles still flatten it — angels, or worse the old “sons of Israel” move that belongs to Deuteronomy 32:8, not Genesis 6. Tell them the English in their hand is a grandchild of the Masoretic Hebrew. Qumran lets us check that grandchild against copies a thousand years older. Where they agree, we can lock it. Genesis 6:1–4 is that kind of agreement. Where they don’t (Deuteronomy 32:8, next week), we say so. Targums that say “sons of nobles” at Genesis 6 are later smoothing: name it, don’t follow it.

In the room: hold up their English Bible, name where it came from, then open Job 1:6 and Genesis 6:2 in Hebrew so בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים is not a Sethite guess. Do not let them hear “sons of Israel” here. Do not send this chain in GroupMe. The guys’ page does not need a versions lecture.

teacherOnly.label: teacher method — open the file; do not dump it on the guys
p: The full brief is not this JSON. On this teacher view open “Why these books / where English comes from,” or open teacher-week2-canon.md. Teacher only. Do not put it on the guys’ home, the student reader, or GroupMe.

Week 1 restore, compact: Genesis 3:15 zera is masculine; hu is a he; the heel suffix is masculine. English “offspring” is thinner. Recap dropped the Latin trap; restore it as already-taught. Circulating Vulgate ipsa (she shall crush) fed Mary-as-crusher piety. Jerome himself, in Hebrew Questions on Genesis, read ipse. Nova Vulgata ipsum. Douay-Rheims she. Not every Mary doctrine hangs on this one word. LXX autos is he. English pew Bibles already have he. Do not rant. The danger is never checking.

If time is short, say this: The book in your hand is English. Hebrew and Aramaic are the source. Genesis 3:15 already named a he who crushes the nachash — zera is masculine, hu is he, the heel suffix is masculine. Some old Latin copies printed she; Jerome himself read he; your pew Bible already has he. Do not rant. Check. Tonight Genesis 6 is sons of God, the same phrase as Job. Qumran has two piles: copies of Moses that confirm him, and extra cave books we label and do not baptize as Torah. Watcher in Scripture is Daniel 4, and those Watchers are holy. Enoch’s class-word is later. Next week Deuteronomy 32:8 is the copy-fight. Romans 11 still stands. Israel is not un-Jewed.

title: Babel and the Nations
theme: nations / allotment / Deuteronomy 32 worldview / Abraham called
big: At Babel Yahweh divides the nations. Deuteronomy 32 describes an allotment under lesser powers; Yahweh keeps Israel as his portion and begins reclaiming the nations through Abraham.
question: What happened to the nations at Babel, and how does Yahweh begin to get them back?
observe: Map Genesis 10 as the table of nations, then 11 as the reason for scattering.
Read Deuteronomy 32:8-9 (compare DSS/LXX sons of God language if you have a note).
Hear Psalm 82: corrupt rulers of the nations will be judged.
Watch Abraham called out so that all families of the earth will be blessed.
Acts 17: God appointed times and boundaries so people might seek him.
teacherMoves: Connect Babel to Pentecost later without dumping week 11.
Keep Psalm 82 as courtroom, not trivia.
Emphasize Abraham as the start of reclaiming nations.
app: Pray for the nations as Yahweh inheritance, not as abandoned territory.
guard: Do not treat other nations as subhuman; the point is spiritual allotment and Yahweh plan to bless all families.
response: Gather the nations, O God, into the blessing of Abraham.

title: Covenant and the Family of Faith
theme: covenant / seed / circumcision / faith counted as righteousness
big: Yahweh cuts covenant with Abraham, promising land, seed, and blessing. Faith is counted as righteousness; the family of faith will bless the nations.
question: What does covenant with Abraham actually promise, and how is it received?
observe: List the promises in Genesis 12, 15, and 17.
Note who walks the pieces in 15: Yahweh binds himself.
Watch the test of the seed in Genesis 22.
Hear Paul: Abraham believed God.
Ask how Gentile believers are grafted into this family without becoming a different people of God.
teacherMoves: Draw a simple covenant chart: parties, promises, sign.
Read Romans 4 after Genesis 15.
Keep Isaac as seed, not as a morality play only.
app: Trust the God who swears by himself when fulfillment looks delayed.
guard: Do not flatten covenant into a generic self-help contract.
response: Count us in Abraham family by faith in the promised Seed.

title: Exodus and Sinai
theme: deliverance / Passover / Torah / kingdom of priests
big: Yahweh redeems Israel from slavery, judges the gods of Egypt, and brings a people to Sinai to be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.
question: Why does Yahweh save Israel, and what kind of people does Sinai form?
observe: Name the contest with Pharaoh and with Egypt gods.
Trace blood, lamb, and firstborn in Passover.
Hear 19:4-6 before the Ten Words.
Watch the golden calf as covenant breach and Moses intercession.
Connect 1 Peter 2: the priestly people now includes the nations in Messiah.
teacherMoves: Keep Passover as rescue unto vocation.
Do not skip the calf: holiness is gift and demand.
Preview tabernacle next week.
app: Live as a delivered priestly people, not as people still owned by old masters.
guard: Do not treat Torah as a ladder to earn rescue; rescue comes first.
response: You brought us out on eagles wings. Make us holy as you are holy.

title: Presence and Holiness
big: Yahweh dwells in the midst of Israel. Sacred space, priesthood, and Day of Atonement teach how a holy God can live with an unholy people.
question: How can Yahweh live among a people without destroying them?
observe: Eden echoes: east, cherubim, gold, gardens, lamp.
Trace who may approach and how.
Watch two goats on the Day of Atonement.
Hear be holy for I am holy in ordinary neighbor-love (Lev 19).
Hebrews 9: Messiah enters the true tent with his own blood.
teacherMoves: Sketch the courts; keep it simple.
Connect sacred space back to Eden and forward to John 1:14.
Guardrail: holiness is not fussiness; it is fitness for presence.
app: Practice holiness as nearness to God that shows up in how you treat neighbors.
guard: Do not treat Leviticus as primitive leftovers. It is about presence.
response: Dwell among us, Holy One. Cleanse us that we may draw near.

title: David and the Faithful King
theme: king / Zion / covenant with David / messianic hope
big: Yahweh chooses a king after his heart and covenants with David: an everlasting throne. The faithful king will embody Israel vocation and crush the rebel powers.
student: 1 Samuel 16-17; 2 Samuel 7; Psalm 2; Psalm 89; Psalm 110; Isaiah 11:1-10
question: What kind of king does Yahweh promise, and why does Israel need one?
observe: Contrast Saul and David as kinds of rule.
List the Davidic promises in 2 Samuel 7.
Read Psalm 2 and 110 as royal/messianic.
Isaiah 11: Spirit-anointed branch who judges righteously.
Ask how giant-slaying (Goliath) echoes seed vs serpent without forcing every detail.
teacherMoves: Keep 2 Samuel 7 as the hub.
Let the psalms preach.
Preview a greater Son of David.
app: Give allegiance to the king Yahweh anoints, not to whatever power looks impressive.
guard: Do not baptize modern politics as the Davidic throne.
response: Let the Son of David reign; teach us to love his rule.

title: Exile and Prophetic Hope
theme: exile / remnant / new covenant / dry bones / return
big: Because of covenant unfaithfulness Israel is expelled from the land, repeating Eden exile. The prophets promise a new covenant, a new heart, and a return under Yahweh own rule.
student: 2 Kings 17:5-23; 2 Kings 24-25; Jeremiah 31; Ezekiel 36-37; Daniel 7; Isaiah 40:1-11
question: What does exile mean, and what hope does Yahweh speak into it?
observe: Name causes of exile in 2 Kings 17.
New covenant: law written on the heart.
Water, Spirit, new heart in Ezekiel 36.
Dry bones: resurrection of a people.
Daniel 7: one like a son of man receives the kingdom.
teacherMoves: Link exile to Genesis 3 geographically and theologically.
Do not end in despair; read the hope texts aloud.
Daniel 7 sets up Jesus favorite title.
app: When you are living with the consequences of unfaithfulness, hear the God who still speaks return.
guard: Do not treat exile as only ancient geopolitics. It is sacred-space loss.
response: Give us a new heart. Bring us home.

title: Jesus, the Faithful Son and Last Adam
theme: incarnation / Son / last Adam / wilderness victory
big: Jesus is Israel in one person and the last Adam: faithful Son where Adam and Israel failed. He recaptures sacred vocation and withstands the rebel.
question: How is Jesus both true human and the one who succeeds where Adam and Israel failed?
observe: Word became flesh and tabernacled among us.
Genealogy and baptism: beloved Son.
Wilderness: three tests vs Eden and vs Israel in the desert.
Last Adam in Romans 5.
Hebrews 2: he shares flesh and blood to destroy the one who has the power of death.
teacherMoves: Read the temptation beside Genesis 3.
Keep fully God and fully human without a philosophy lecture.
Set up week 10: this faithful life goes to a cross.
app: Follow the Son into the wilderness: answer the rebel with Yahweh word.
guard: Do not treat Jesus as a mere moral example. He is the last Adam who represents us.
response: Faithful Son, live in us what we could not live alone.

title: Cross and Resurrection
big: At the cross Jesus dies for sin and disarms the powers. In the resurrection he is firstfruits of new creation and public victory over death.
question: What happened at the cross and the empty tomb for us and for the powers?
observe: Servant song: bearing, substitution, many accounted righteous.
Temple veil / centurion confession.
Mary at the tomb: new-garden echoes.
Paul creed: died, buried, raised, appeared.
Colossians 2: powers stripped and publicly shamed.
teacherMoves: Hold penal, victorious, and new-creation notes together.
Do not skip resurrection; Friday is not the end.
Keep it pastoral: this is for sinners in the room.
app: Boast only in the cross; live as people already on the resurrection side of history.
guard: Do not reduce the cross to inspirational suffering or the resurrection to a metaphor.
response: Lamb who was slain, you are worthy. Raise us with you.

title: Spirit, Assembly, and the Nations Reclaimed
theme: Pentecost / Spirit / ekklesia / table of nations reversed
big: The Spirit is poured out; Babel is reversed; the assembly becomes the place where the nations are reclaimed as Yahweh inheritance in Messiah.
student: Acts 1-2; Acts 10; Acts 13:44-49; Joel 2:28-32; Ephesians 2:11-3:13; Revelation 7:9-12
question: What does the Spirit do to Yahweh people and to the nations?
observe: Pentecost languages vs Babel scattering.
Peter: this Jesus, Lord and Messiah.
Cornelius: Gentiles receive the Spirit.
Ephesians 2: one new humanity, dividing wall down.
Revelation 7: every nation before the throne.
teacherMoves: Name Babel reversal explicitly.
Keep church as assembly, not a building.
Mission is reclaiming allotted nations, not hobby.
app: Speak the good news across whatever boundary you usually will not cross.
guard: Do not treat the Spirit as private energy detached from the nations story.
response: Come, Holy Spirit. Make us one people for the sake of the many.

title: Serpent Judged, Eden Restored, New Earth
theme: final judgment / new Jerusalem / tree of life / God with us
big: The rebel is judged, death dies, and Eden is more than restored: a garden-city where God dwells with humanity on a new earth. Image-bearers finally rule as they were made to.
question: How does the story end, and what are humans for in the end?
observe: Creation groaning for the revealing of the children of God.
Last enemy: death. All enemies under his feet.
Serpent/devil thrown down; death and Hades judged.
New heaven and new earth; God with them.
Tree of life, river, face of God, they will reign forever.
teacherMoves: Close the loop to week 1 vocation.
Keep hope embodied: new earth, not escape.
Send them out with a charge, not only a chart.
app: Practice hope: plant, reconcile, worship as people who will reign on a renewed earth.
guard: Do not swap the Bible ending for a disembodied heaven-only script.
response: Even so, come Lord Jesus. Restore all things.
